title: Colourwork square shawl
subtitle: A centre-out DK square with a stranded colourwork star radiating from the centre.
excerpt: A square shawl in DK wool worked centre-out with a 4-section stranded colourwork star pattern radiating outward along each diagonal. The star motif grows with the shawl as each section widens. Finished size approximately 110 × 110 cm when blocked. About 300 g of main colour plus 150 g of contrast.
sourceNotes: Centre-out square construction appears in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 2nd series (1886), §Shawls. The radiating star colourwork motif in a centre-out square is a modern design application of the traditional construction; there is no single period source for this specific combination.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: In stranded colourwork, the colour carried consistently below the other in the working hand. It sits slightly lower in the stitch and reads more prominently. Consistency in dominant colour assignment matters more than which colour is dominant.

content.text: A centre-out DK square with a stranded star motif radiating from the centre along each diagonal. Finished size approximately 110 × 110 cm.

The star motif is introduced 8 stitches from each corner marker once the sections are wide enough to carry the colourwork pattern cleanly. The star arm grows by 2 stitches on each side every 4 rows as the square widens. Keep the
dominant colour
consistent throughout. Budget about 300 g of MC and 150 g of CC in DK wool.
What you need

items.name: Main colour (MC)
items.qty: About 300 g (660 m / 720 yards) of DK-weight yarn

items.name: Contrast colour (CC)
items.qty: About 150 g (330 m / 360 yards) of DK-weight yarn in a contrasting colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 100 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. Stranded sections run about 2 stitches tighter per 10 cm than garter; the star arms will be very slightly narrower than the garter background. This is expected and correct. At 110 × 110 cm finished size, the cast-on is 8 stitches and the square grows by 8 stitches per RS row for approximately 240 RS rows.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on and early growth

Cast on 8 stitches in MC. Place markers after sts 2, 4, 6. Work the standard centre-out RS row: *k to marker, yo, SM, yo; repeat from * 3 more times, k to end. Work in MC garter until each quarter holds at least 20 stitches (approximately 10 RS rows).
Star arm colourwork

From row 11 onward, work the star arm in each quarter: the central 4 stitches of each quarter (2 either side of the corner marker) are worked in CC on RS rows; the surrounding body stitches remain in MC. Every 4 rows, extend the star arm 1 stitch further from the corner marker in each direction: by row 50 the star arm spans 10 stitches across each quarter.
RS colourwork row: *k to star arm position in MC, work star arm stitches in CC, continue in MC to marker, yo, SM, yo; repeat from * for all 4 quarters.
WS row: k all sts in their respective colours (CC over CC, MC over MC).
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off in MC, breaking CC before the bind-off row.
Stitch count check-ins
After 60 RS rows: 8 + 480 = 488 stitches. Side length approximately 27 cm. Each star arm spans approximately 6 stitches.
After 180 RS rows: 1,448 stitches. Side length approximately 82 cm. Each star arm spans approximately 18 stitches across the corner diagonal.
Common faults
Star arm width not growing evenly: the arm expansion (add 1 stitch each side every 4 rows) was applied inconsistently. Mark the expansion rows explicitly in a row counter.
Floats too long at wide arm sections: once the CC arm spans more than 5 stitches, catch the float on the WS mid-span to avoid a long loose strand.
Blocking
Wet-block to 110 × 110 cm. Check CC for dye bleed before soaking. Pin all four corners to the stated dimensions.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water. Lay flat to dry. At 110 cm the square needs a large flat surface; the floor works if the mat is too small.
What to try next
Add a second CC colour for the outermost star arm layer so the star fades from CC1 near the centre to CC2 near the edges, creating a three-colour concentric star.
